actions.action: Let the cut ends callous and dry before putting the cutting back in water
Submerge the cutting to just above the node
Add pothos cuttings to the jar as a natural rooting aid
Cut off the leaf at the lowest node if present
Move the cutting to a bigger glass, such as a mason jar, with the nodes fully covered
Change the water at least once a week
Add a little hydrogen peroxide to the prop water
Alternatively, cut the stem closer to the node and root it in soil with lots of perlite
Seal the cut with candle wax after cutting with a disinfected knife

verdict.reason: The answer blames callousing, node depth and rooting hormone, and never identifies the frequent water changes or the moss as the problem; several comments even urge frequent water changes, which would prolong the actual cause.
